_note: A starter library, not a correct one. Every angle-bracketed name is a placeholder — <COI_REQUEST>, <IL_PAYMENT_STAGING>, <team> — and must be replaced with what your systems actually call things before anybody follows these. Every runbook here is a draft on purpose: approve one only when somebody who knows the system has read it. Import from Menu → Setup → Runbooks → Import library.

runbooks.title: COI letter does not generate, but the API returned success
triggers: regencoi went through but no letter
steps: Confirm which policy number(s) the user actually asked for — take them from the request, not from memory.
Re-run the regeneration in Swagger for those policy numbers and note the response. A 200 here does not mean a letter was produced; see the Imaging profile.
Run the checks below. They tell you whether the source data the letter needs is present and in a state the template can render.
If a row is missing or its status is not one the template accepts, this is a data problem, not an imaging problem. Do not keep re-running the generation.
If the data is present and correct and the letter still does not appear, capture the request id and the exact time, then escalate.
Reply to the user with which of the two it was, so they know whether to wait or to chase another team.
runbooks.checks:
Replace the bracketed names with your real ones.

```sql
-- is the request even there, and what state is it in
SELECT policy_no, status, created_on, letter_id
FROM   <COI_REQUEST>
WHERE  policy_no IN ('<policy>')
ORDER  BY created_on DESC;

-- did the letter get written at all
SELECT letter_id, policy_no, generated_on, file_path
FROM   <COI_LETTER>
WHERE  policy_no IN ('<policy>');

-- the fields the template will not render without
SELECT policy_no, insured_name, sum_insured, effective_date, expiry_date
FROM   <POLICY_MASTER>
WHERE  policy_no IN ('<policy>');
```

A row in <COI_REQUEST> with no matching <COI_LETTER> row is the signature of this problem. A NULL in any of the last four fields is usually the reason.
runbooks.escalation:
Data missing in <POLICY_MASTER> → <team that owns policy data>, with the policy number and which field is null.
Data present and letter still missing → <Imaging owner>, with the request id and the timestamp.
P1 only if it blocks an issuance deadline the same day.

runbooks.title: Payment not flowing to IL enquiry
triggers: payment not flowing to il enquiry
steps: Get the receipt or transaction reference and the payment date from the user. A policy number alone is not enough to trace one payment.
Confirm the payment actually settled at the gateway before looking anywhere downstream — an unsettled payment has nothing to flow.
Check whether the transaction reached the staging table (below). This splits the problem in two: it never arrived, or it arrived and did not post.
If it never arrived, the break is upstream of IL — collect the gateway reference and escalate to the payment team.
If it arrived but did not post, read the error on the staging row. Most are a policy in a state that will not accept a payment, or a mismatched amount.
Tell the user which side it broke on and what happens next. Do not tell them to 'wait and check again' without saying what you found.
runbooks.checks:
```sql
-- did it arrive
SELECT txn_ref, policy_no, amount, status, error_msg, received_on
FROM   <IL_PAYMENT_STAGING>
WHERE  txn_ref = '<reference>'
   OR  policy_no = '<policy>'
ORDER  BY received_on DESC;

-- did it post
SELECT policy_no, receipt_no, amount, posted_on
FROM   <IL_RECEIPT>
WHERE  policy_no = '<policy>'
ORDER  BY posted_on DESC;
```

No staging row → it never arrived. Staging row with an error_msg → read it before doing anything else.
runbooks.escalation:
Never arrived → <payment gateway team> with the gateway reference and the settlement time.
Arrived with an error → fix per the error if it is a known one, otherwise <IL owner>.
Raise to P1 if it is a lapse-risk policy near its grace date.

runbooks.title: User asks for a report that has not refreshed
steps: Ask which report and which date they expected to see. 'The report is wrong' is not something you can act on.
Check when the feeding job last completed successfully.
If the job failed, read the failure before re-running it — a job that failed on bad data will fail again the same way.
If the job succeeded but the data is still missing, the gap is upstream of the job.
Tell the user the date the data is actually good to, rather than only that you are looking into it.
runbooks.checks:
```sql
SELECT job_name, run_date, status, rows_loaded, message
FROM   <ETL_JOB_LOG>
WHERE  job_name = '<job>'
ORDER  BY run_date DESC;
```
runbooks.escalation:
Job failing repeatedly on the same row → <data team>.
Upstream source empty → the team that owns the source, not reporting.

profiles.facts: Generates and stores policy documents, including the Confirmation of Insurance (COI) letter. Regeneration is normally done through Swagger by passing one or more policy numbers.
profiles.quirks:
The regenCOI endpoint returns 200 whether or not a letter was actually produced. It reports that the request was accepted, not that the document exists. This is the single most common source of confusion on this system: staff click generate, see success, and assume the letter is there.

So a successful call proves nothing. Always confirm the letter row exists before telling a user it is done.

When the source data is incomplete the template silently renders nothing rather than raising an error.
profiles.tables:
<COI_REQUEST>   one row per regeneration request
<COI_LETTER>    one row per letter actually produced
<POLICY_MASTER> the fields the template reads

profiles.facts: Takes premium payments from the gateway and posts them to IL, where they become visible in enquiry.
profiles.quirks:
There are two hops, and they fail differently. Gateway → staging is where payments go missing entirely. Staging → IL is where they arrive but do not post, usually because the policy is in a state that will not accept a payment or the amount does not match what was expected.

Always establish which hop broke before escalating. Escalating to the wrong team costs a day.
profiles.tables:
<IL_PAYMENT_STAGING> arrived, not yet posted
<IL_RECEIPT>         posted
